dial.summary: 5/8 indicators supportive entering November 11 — October CPI printed hot at 0.4% MoM (vs 0.3% consensus, no official YoY due to 2025 shutdown base distortion), pushing DXY back to 102.07 and sealing December FOMC hike expectations; real yields ticked to 2.66% (Nov 9) but remain on a 4-week downtrend from ~2.90% on Oct 10; BTC consolidating at ~$74–76K post the November 8–9 liquidation flush with neutral funding (0.0087%), confirming the accumulation pattern holds while the market digests the inflation surprise ahead of PPI (Nov 13) and FOMC Minutes (Nov 18).

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: MacroMicro G4 aggregate (US/Euro Zone/China/Japan) holds at ~$104.3T as of September 2026 (104,317B); October G4 data not yet published — MacroMicro typically updates mid-month following the reference month, so October G4 update expected mid-November 2026; US M2 at $23.4T in Sep 2026 (+5.7% YoY per Macrotrends/FRED, Mises Institute confirms money-supply growth rising to multi-year high as Fed resumed QE); 4-week Aug→Sep change +$0.64T (+0.6%) exceeds flat threshold — trend UP; status supportive (4-week trend up, no YoY contraction); held unchanged from Nov 9 run — October G4 data publication pending mid-November 2026.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: October 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.5% (released November 2, 2026), beating consensus 54.6%, up 1.0pp from September's 54.5%; 10th consecutive expansion month; Production sub-index 59.0 (highest since Nov 2021), New Orders 55.5, Prices 75.2 (9th consecutive above 70); 4-week trend UP (Sep 54.5 → Oct 55.5, +1.0pp); status supportive (above 50 and rising); next ISM Manufacturing release December 1, 2026 (November data); value confirmed November 10 — monthly series, October 55.5 is the current reading.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY spot 102.07 as of November 10, 2026 close (Investing.com; Trading Economics shows 102.36); DXY rallied sharply on November 10 after October CPI printed +0.4% MoM vs +0.3% consensus (BLS release), cementing December FOMC hike expectations; prior close Nov 9: 101.99; 4-week trend UP — from ~101.5–101.8 on October 10 to 102.07 on November 10, net change ~+0.57%, exceeding the 0.5% flat threshold; status headwind (DXY above 100 — must fall below 97.5 for supportive); FRED DTWEXBGS network-restricted in this environment.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: 10-year TIPS real yield (DFII10) at 2.66% on November 9, 2026 (Federal Reserve H.15 release; Nov 6: 2.63%, Nov 5: 2.60%); 3-day uptick of +6bps but 4-week trend remains DOWN — from ~2.85–2.90% around October 10 to 2.66% on November 9, approximately -20 to -25bps; Nov 10 close not yet published (expected from FRED next business day — hot CPI +0.4% MoM may push real yields modestly higher); status supportive (falling 4-week trend — headwind requires BOTH rising trend AND above 2% simultaneously; value above 2% but 4-week trend still down, only one condition met); FRED API network-restricted in this environment.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: 2s10s spread confirmed at +35bps as of November 6, 2026 close (multiple sources: yieldcurve.pro, 247wallst, sofrrate.com; 10Y: ~4.86–4.95%, 2Y: ~4.46–4.61% per various sources; meaterm.com cites +0.38pp on Nov 5); down 3bps on the day Nov 6 as the front end repriced post-NFP; 4-week trend FLAT — from approximately +30–32bps around October 7 to +35bps on November 6, approximately +3–5bps within the flat threshold; 52-week range 20–74bps; status neutral (positive and recovering but not sustainably steepening on a 4-week basis).

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,748,145M ($6.748T) for week ended November 4, 2026 (FRED updated November 5; confirmed by 247wallst Nov 8: 'Fed's $6.75 Trillion Balance Sheet Is Growing Again'; next H.4.1 release November 12 for week ended November 11); prior readings: Oct 28 $6,745,635M, Oct 21 $6,753,604M, Oct 14 $6,755,639M; 4-week change Oct 7 → Nov 4: balance sheet oscillating in a narrow ~$10B band, essentially flat; balance sheet stabilized post-QT-pause (QT ended December 2025); YoY +2.4% from ~$6.59T; 247wallst notes the Fed has rolled over maturing bonds and bought Treasury bills to keep reserves ample; status supportive (flat, no aggressive QT); FRED API network-restricted — WALCL confirmed via web search corroboration.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: CoinGlass OI-weighted BTC perp funding rate 0.0087% (position-weighted), volume-weighted 0.0081%, per ChainCatcher citing CoinGlass (Nov 8–9, 2026); exchange-level snapshots: Bybit 0.0112%, Binance 0.0095% (CoinGlass live pages); BTC experienced a sharp drop to $73,761–$74K on November 8–9 with $1.04B+ in leveraged-long liquidations (CoinDesk/CryptoCatcher citing CoinGlass); 'drop and pop' pattern observed as price recovered; 30-day trend FLAT — oscillating 0.005–0.010% per 8h; late-September rates were near zero/negative; status supportive (well below 0.04% headwind threshold); the post-liquidation flush returning to near-neutral funding confirms no speculative excess, consistent with accumulation; coinglass.com network-restricted for direct API access.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap $290.8B as of November 10, 2026 (DefiLlama; USDT ~60.79% share); stablecoin.com (Nov 5): $286.3B; The Central Bulletin/DefiLlama (Nov 5): $295.21B; total crypto market cap unclear — Coinbird appears to show 10.90% stablecoin dominance but date unconfirmed; TOTAL estimated ~$2.60–2.67T; value held at 11.2% (Nov 9) due to conflicting total market cap sources post-BTC liquidation event; 30-day trend UP — October 1 dominance ~10.2% ($291B/$2.86T), rising as TOTAL declined while stablecoins held; status neutral — headwind requires rising dominance AND rising TOTAL simultaneously; TOTAL declined from Oct 1 level ($2.60T vs $2.86T) so headwind condition not met, but dominance is not falling so supportive condition not met; value unchanged pending confirmation.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended November 8, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL releases weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET on Thursday November 12 (normal Thursday schedule — Veterans Day is Wednesday Nov 11, not Thursday); first labor pulse following the strong October NFP (+165K, unemployment 4.1%) and the hot October CPI (+0.4% MoM, Nov 10); a claims print below 215K would reinforce the December hike narrative, while a spike above 230K would reintroduce labor-market cooling debate; Fed H.4.1 balance sheet release (WALCL, week ended Nov 11) also expected this day.

upcoming.title: PPI (October 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS releases October 2026 Producer Price Index at 8:30 AM ET; completes the November inflation picture alongside CPI (Oct headline +0.4% MoM, released Nov 10 — hot vs +0.3% consensus); September PPI was +6.3% YoY and ISM Manufacturing Prices remains elevated at 75.2 (9th consecutive print above 70); a hot PPI print would amplify the December hike case; oil's ~6% drop to $85 on Nov 9 may moderate the energy component of headline PPI.

upcoming.title: US Retail Sales (October 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau releases October 2026 Advance Monthly Retail Trade Survey at 8:30 AM ET; September retail sales were +0.8% MoM (well above the +0.3% forecast); a print above +0.5% MoM would add to the already-strong December hike case after the hot October CPI (+0.4% MoM); a miss near 0% would add soft-landing ambiguity but is unlikely to outweigh the inflation surprise; this is the last major growth read before the FOMC blackout period begins November 28.

upcoming.title: Industrial Production (October 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve releases October 2026 Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization (G.17) at 9:15 AM ET; September industrial production rose +0.4% MoM; a continued expansion would corroborate the October ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.5 (10th consecutive expansion month); note: the Fed plans an annual G.17 revision release on November 24, so this reading may be subject to revision.

upcoming.title: Housing Starts (October 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau releases October 2026 New Residential Construction at 8:30 AM ET; elevated mortgage rates (30Y near 7.1%, 10Y at ~4.86%) and real yields at 2.66% (down from 2.90% but still historically high) continue to pressure housing affordability; after the hot CPI print sealing higher-for-longer expectations, a sharp drop in permits would underscore the housing drag on Q4 2026 growth.

upcoming.title: FOMC Minutes — October 27–28 Meeting
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve releases minutes of the October 27–28 FOMC meeting at 2:00 PM ET; the Fed held at 3.75%–4.00% (vote 10–2) at that meeting; minutes will reveal member views on the threshold for a December 9 hike given elevated ISM Prices (75.2) and Iran-war supply shocks; the November 10 hot CPI print (+0.4% MoM) arrived after the October meeting, so the minutes predate it — markets will read them against the new inflation reality; FOMC blackout period begins November 28.
